```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

`fit()` runs the sampler through its stages (preburn, burn, adapt, sample) and stops each
one when its Rhat rule is met or its try budget is used up. For most models that is all you
need. Some fits are hard: hundreds of subjects with a few extreme ones, race models with many
effects on rates, DDMs with across-trial variability. In those, Rhat can pass with too few
effective draws, a chain can sit in a degenerate region with the same Rhat as the others, a
subject can have two posterior modes that the group-level Rhat never sees, and a fit that
will never converge can run for hours.

Two functions cover this:

- **`hardfit()`** runs the same sampler as `fit()`, one check at a time, under a stricter stop
  rule, replaces chains that have gone wrong, stops early when a fit will not converge, and
  records how the fit ended.
- **`diagnose()`** reads any fitted object — from `fit()` or `hardfit()` — and says which of
  five outcomes you are looking at, why, and what to do next.

This vignette is about using them. The rules themselves and the evidence behind the
thresholds are in the last section.

## Quick start

```{r}
emc <- make_emc(data, design, n_chains = 6)
emc <- hardfit(emc)
diagnose(emc)
```

Six chains rather than three: the chain replacement needs healthy chains to copy from, and a
subject with two posterior modes is detected only when at least one chain finds each mode
(with 3 chains it is missed in a quarter to a third of runs, with 6 in about one in ten).
`hardfit()` prints a note when a hierarchical object has fewer than 6 chains.

The defaults are the ones below; a fit that returns `diagnose(emc)$class == "met"` has
passed all of them.

## Running a hard fit

### The stop rule

`hardfit()` ends the sample stage when, on one set of kept draws, every criterion that is on
holds:

| argument | default | criterion |
|---|---|---|
| `max_gd` | 1.1 (1.05 for `type = "single"`) | the rule's Rhat is below this |
| `gd_quantile` | .99 (1 for `type = "single"`) | the rule reads this quantile of the subject-level Rhats (and every group-level Rhat); 1 is the plain maximum |
| `min_ess` | 100 | the smallest effective sample size over the group means and log group SDs, summed over chains |
| `max_ll_gap` | 100 | the chains' summed subject log-likelihoods lie within this many units |
| `max_subj_spread` | 15 | every subject's chain log-likelihoods lie within this many units |
| `iter` | 1000 | the stage holds at least this many new draws per chain |

`NULL` turns one of the first five off. Everything is an argument:

```{r}
emc <- hardfit(emc, max_gd = 1.1, gd_quantile = .99, min_ess = 100, max_ll_gap = 100,
               max_subj_spread = 15, iter = 1000, step_size = 100, max_tries = 40)
```

`step_size` is the number of draws per chain between checks, and `max_tries` the number of
checks before an unmet stage ends (`fit()`'s default is 20). An unmet stage ends with a
warning pointing to `diagnose()`, and keeps every draw.

When the rule fails on all the stage's draws but passes with the first third dropped, the
shorter history is used only if every other criterion then passes too; the drop is recorded.
Otherwise nothing is thrown away.

### Chain replacement

`cull = TRUE` (the default) watches, at every burn and sample check, for a chain held in a
different region from the others: its summed log-likelihood 200 units and 5 within-chain
spreads below the best chain's, for two checks running, and either 1,000 units below or also
lower on its own log posterior. Such a chain has its state replaced by a copy of a healthy
chain's (kernel settings included). Burn may do this twice at its checks and once more at
its end; sample does it once and then restarts its kept draws. Replacing a chain's state
during warm-up changes a starting point, not the posterior.

`cull = FALSE` turns it off; a list adjusts it, for example a more patient rule:

```{r}
emc <- hardfit(emc, cull = list(chain_gap = 500, persistence = 3))
```

The fields are `chain_gap` (200), `chain_z` (5), `persistence` (2), `lp_guard_below` (1000),
`max_culls` (1 in sample, 2 in burn), `reburn` (100 iterations after a sample-stage
replacement before the kept draws restart), `window` and `min_window` (the draws the
comparison uses; by default the last two thirds of the stage, at least 500 in sample and 250
in burn).

### The early stop

`abort_gd = 1.5, abort_try = 20`: at the 20th sample-stage check, a fit whose rule Rhat is
still above 1.5 ends there, with a warning, and is recorded as `aborted`. In replays of 46
fits in that position none met the rule later, so continuing spends compute for nothing.
`abort_gd = NULL` turns it off.

### The other stages

Burn runs under `fit()`'s mean-Rhat rule, one check at a time with the chain replacement
between checks; `burn = list(mean_gd = 1.1, max_tries = 40)` sets its threshold and budget.
Preburn and adapt run exactly as in `fit()`. The sampler, its kernel and its draws are
`fit()`'s throughout: `hardfit()` only decides when to stop, which chains to replace and
what to record.

### Continuing, saving, cores

A call on a fitted object continues its sample stage: another `iter` draws per chain are
added and the rule is re-checked, with the earlier record kept under `stop_record$previous`.
A fit started with `fit()` can be continued with `hardfit()` and the reverse; the adapted
kernel is kept either way.

```{r}
emc <- hardfit(emc)                                   # continue
emc <- hardfit(emc, fileName = "fit.RData")           # saved after every check
emc <- hardfit(emc, cores_for_chains = 6, cores_per_chain = 4)
emc <- hardfit("fit.RData")                           # resume from the file
```

`fileName`, `cores_for_chains`, `cores_per_chain`, `particle_factor`, `search_width`,
`on_singular` and `history_proposals` mean what they mean in `fit()`.

### Single-subject fits

For `type = "single"` the rule reads the maximum Rhat over the subject's parameters, at
1.05, and the effective-size floor applies to those parameters; the subject-spread criterion
does not apply. The likelihood-gap veto and the chain replacement work as above.

## Reading the progress line

Burn prints `fit()`'s line with the chain replacements added; each sample-stage check prints
one line with every criterion on it. From a 518-subject LBA fit with 6 chains:

```
Running burn stage
[burn | try=1 | iters=100 | Mean Rhat=1.412] Duration: 1.2 min - ETA (to max_tries): 46.8 min
[burn | try=2 | iters=200 | Mean Rhat=1.216] Duration: 1.2 min - ETA (to max_tries): 47.3 min
[burn | try=3 | iters=200 | Mean Rhat=1.067 (first 100 draws dropped)] Duration: 1.4 min - ...
Running adapt stage
...
Running sample stage
[sample | try=1 | iters=100 | Rhat=2.126 (rule; max 8.431) | min ESS=36 (v_CIcong) |
 LL gap=51 | subject spread=5.9 (s331; 2 > 5)] Duration: 1.3 min - ETA (to max_tries): 11.6 min
[sample | try=2 | iters=200 | Rhat=2.260 (rule; max 8.358) | min ESS=62 (v_CIcong) |
 LL gap=66 | subject spread=5.9 (s331; 1 > 5)] Duration: 1.3 min - ETA (to max_tries): 10.1 min
...
[sample | try=10 | iters=1000 | Rhat=1.604 (rule; max 7.767) | min ESS=73 (lsd:v_iMd) |
 LL gap=24 | subject spread=5.3 (s331; 1 > 5)] Duration: 1.4 min - ETA (to max_tries): 0.0 s
Warning message:
Max tries reached before all stopping criteria were met (see diagnose(emc)).
```

(each check is one line; wrapped here for the page)

- `Rhat=2.126 (rule; max 8.431)`: the value the stop rule compares with 1.1, and the plain
  maximum over every parameter. When the two differ by this much, one subject is far from the
  others on one parameter; the rule has put it in the top 1% and is reading the rest.
- `min ESS=36 (v_CIcong)`: the smallest effective sample size and its parameter (`lsd:` marks
  a log group SD). The parameter says where mixing is slow — here a rate effect, typically the
  direction along which the chains disagree.
- `LL gap=51`: the largest difference between chains in summed log-likelihood. Healthy fits sit
  under 40; the veto is 100; a replacement needs 200.
- `subject spread=5.9 (s331; 2 > 5)`: the subject whose chains disagree most, its spread in
  log-likelihood units, and how many subjects exceed 5. A spread above 15 is a subject with two
  modes and chains in both.

A chain replacement prints on the line of the check it happened at:

```
[burn | try=4 | iters=400 | Mean Rhat=1.979 |
 chain 2 respawned from chain 5 (log-likelihood 8986 below, z = 74.7)] ...
[sample | try=6 | iters=100 | Rhat=1.31 (rule; max 2.1) | ... |
 chain 3 respawned from chain 1 (log-likelihood 412 below, z = 9.3);
 sample stage restarted] ...
```

and the early stop as a warning naming the check, the Rhat and the threshold.

## diagnose()

```{r}
d <- diagnose(emc)
d
```

`diagnose()` works on any fitted object because it reads the draws; a record written by
`hardfit()` is used when there is one. The print is one screen. For the fit whose progress
line is above:

```
Class: ridge_only, rule Rhat still falling (sample stage, 1000 draws per chain, 6 chains)
Rule Rhat 1.604 (threshold 1.1; plain max 7.767) | min ESS 73 (lsd:v_iMd) |
 rhat_b 1.369, rhat_ident 1.032
LL gap 24 (worst chain 6) | subject spread 5.3 (s331; 1 > 5)
Drift (first vs last third, in IQRs; se): mu 0.63 (0.13), alpha 0.37 (0.06),
 LL 0.11 (0.06), subj_ll 0.19 (0.05)

Chains (median summed log-likelihood; gap to the best chain, z in within-chain spreads;
 own log posterior lower than the others'; would be culled):
 chain median_ll    gap      z median_lp lp_lower flagged
     1     62429 22.619 0.4243     65547    FALSE   FALSE
     2     62443  8.439 0.1583     64834     TRUE   FALSE
     3     62442  9.224 0.1731     64939     TRUE   FALSE
     4     62451  0.000 0.0000     65229    FALSE   FALSE
     5     62433 18.597 0.3489     64807     TRUE   FALSE
     6     62427 24.219 0.4544     65251    FALSE   FALSE

Subjects with spread > 5 (1):
 subject spread best worst
    s331   5.27    3     5

Record: met FALSE, tries 10, restarts 0, culls 0, discards 0

The chains agree on every identified quantity and disagree along a direction the data do
not fix. Report the identified quantities (rhat_ident near 1); reparameterise or tighten
the prior on the weakly identified parameter. Continuing helps only while the rule Rhat is
still falling. The rule Rhat fell over the last three checks: one continuation is worth
trying.
```

Line by line:

1. **The class** (one of five, below), whether the rule Rhat is still falling, and what was read.
2. **The stop rule and its statistics.** Two are not on the progress line and are the most
   useful for an unmet fit. `rhat_b` is the Rhat of the group means projected on the direction
   along which the chain means differ most: how far apart the chains are. `rhat_ident` is the
   Rhat projected on the direction the posterior pins down most tightly — the combination of
   parameters the data identify best. `rhat_ident` near 1 with `rhat_b` large means the chains
   agree on everything the data determine and disagree along a direction the data do not.
3. **The likelihood comparison**: the chain furthest below the best, and the widest subject.
4. **Drift**: is the posterior still *moving* during the stage? For the group means (`mu`,
   maximum over parameters), the subject parameters (`alpha`, .99 quantile), the summed
   log-likelihood (`LL`) and the subject log-likelihoods (`subj_ll`, .99 quantile), the draws
   of all chains are pooled and the first third is compared with the last: the shift of the
   median in IQR units, with its Monte Carlo error in brackets. Within about 3 se is noise.
   Parameters drifting while the likelihood does not (here `mu` 0.63 at 5 se, `LL` 0.11 at
   2 se) is the ridge signature: the chains are sliding along a direction the likelihood is
   flat on. `LL` or `subj_ll` drifting well beyond its se means a chain or a subject is still
   changing region.
5. **The chain table**: each chain's median summed log-likelihood over the last two thirds of
   the stage, its gap to the best chain in units and in within-chain spreads (`z`), its own log
   posterior and whether that is below the others' (`lp_lower`), and whether the replacement
   rule would act on it (`flagged`). Here no chain is more than 24 units from the best.
6. **The subject table**, widest spread first, with the chains at either end.
7. **The record**, when the object has one.
8. **What to do next.**

The object behind the print:

```{r}
d$class        # "met", "ess_held", "aborted", "ridge_only" or "region_mode"
d$falling      # TRUE if the rule Rhat fell over the last three checks of an unmet fit
d$next_step    # the advice printed last
d$rule         # rule, max, threshold, quantile, met
d$stats        # ess_min, ess_min_par, rhat_b, rhat_ident, ll_gap, ll_z, ll_worst_chain,
               # subj_spread, subj_spread_n5, subj_spread_subject
d$chains       # the chain table
d$subjects     # the subject table (all subjects)
d$flat         # drift, mcse, ess, worst parameter, for mu, alpha, LL, subj_ll
d$record       # emc[[1]]$stop_record, or NULL
```

The thresholds the class is read against are arguments with the `hardfit()` defaults
(`max_gd`, `gd_quantile`, `min_ess`, `max_ll_gap`, `max_subj_spread`), plus `rhat_ident_max`
(1.1) and `drift_se` (3) for the ridge class, so a fit from `fit()` can be graded under any
rule after the fact:

```{r}
diagnose(emc, min_ess = 200)$class
diagnose(emc, stage = "burn")          # the chain comparison on burn draws
```

### Prior tension

One more line appears when the prior is pulling against the data:

```
Prior tension (posterior mean in prior SDs from the prior mean, beyond 3): v +4.2, t0 -3.6
```

`d$prior` holds, for every group mean (for `type = "single"`, every subject parameter), its
posterior mean in prior SDs from the prior mean; `prior_se = 3` sets the flag. The flag never
changes the class. It matters most with `ridge_only`: along a direction the data leave flat
the prior is what sets the posterior, and a likelihood leaning the other way — a few
log-likelihood units toward low `t0`, say, against a prior whose mean sits several SDs the
other side of every subject — makes two shallow plateaus the chains cannot settle between.
Such a fit continues for hours with the rule Rhat creeping down. `next_step` says so when a
parameter is flagged: check the prior before continuing, and if it was set without thought
for the scale of these data, refit with one that was.

## The five outcomes, and what to do with each

### `met`

```
Class: met (sample stage, 3300 draws per chain, 6 chains)
Rule Rhat 1.085 (threshold 1.1; plain max 1.21) | min ESS 133 (v) |
 rhat_b 1.07, rhat_ident 1.01
LL gap 23 (worst chain 4) | subject spread 3.1 (s105; 0 > 5)
```

Converged under every criterion. Use the fit. `culls > 0` in the record is harmless here: a
chain started badly during warm-up and was replaced.

### `ess_held`: Rhat passed, effective size short

```
Class: ess_held (sample stage, 4000 draws per chain, 6 chains)
Rule Rhat 1.07 (threshold 1.1; plain max 1.18) | min ESS 54 (lsd:B) | ...
Record: met FALSE, tries 40, ...
The chains agree but the effective sample size is short: continue the fit (hardfit(emc))
once or twice.
```

`fit()` would have called this converged. The chains agree, but the group SD of `B` has 54
effective draws, so its posterior median is known to about 0.17 posterior SDs. Continue:

```{r}
emc <- hardfit(emc)
```

Expect the effective size to grow with the draws (0.5–1.5 per 100 draws per chain in slow
fits); once or twice is usually enough.

### `aborted`

```
Class: aborted (sample stage, 2000 draws per chain, 6 chains)
Rule Rhat 2.246 (threshold 1.1; plain max 9.1) | ...
Record: met FALSE, tries 20, aborted at check 20 (rule 2.246 > 1.5), ...
```

Do not continue it. The chain table, `rhat_ident` and the subject table say which of the next
two cases it is; act on the model or the starting points, not the iteration count.

### `ridge_only`

The fit printed in full above. The chains agree on every identified quantity (`rhat_ident`
1.03) and on the likelihood (gap 24, `LL` drift within noise) and still differ along one
direction (`rhat_b` 1.37; `mu` and `alpha` drifting at 5–6 se). To see which direction, look
at the within-chain correlations of the group means:

```{r}
cor(t(emc[[1]]$samples$theta_mu[, emc[[1]]$samples$stage == "sample"]))
```

A pair at −0.99 or beyond is the ridge. In race models it is typically the rate intercept
against its match effect — the rate of the losing accumulator, which few errors leave almost
unidentified. The posterior along that direction is set by the prior, not the data, and no
amount of running makes six chains agree on it quickly.

What to do: report the identified quantities (sums or differences of the correlated pair,
and everything else, all with Rhat near 1) and say the ridge direction is prior-determined;
or reparameterise so the identified combination is a parameter; or tighten the prior on the
weakly identified rate. Continue only while `falling` is `TRUE`, and at most once or twice.

### `region_mode`

Two different things print this class, and the print says which.

**A chain in a worse region.** The same model and data as above, a different seed, fitted
with `fit()` and read afterwards:

```
Class: region_mode (sample stage, 4000 draws per chain, 6 chains)
Rule Rhat 260.953 (threshold 1.1; plain max 260.953) | min ESS 71 (B_CIRincong) |
 rhat_b 334.030, rhat_ident 177.856
LL gap 4394 (worst chain 2) | subject spread 86.9 (s304; 389 > 5)
Drift (first vs last third, in IQRs; se): mu 0.47 (2.17), alpha 0.21 (0.06),
 LL 0.03 (0.06), subj_ll 0.27 (0.05)

Chains (...):
 chain median_ll      gap       z median_lp lp_lower flagged
     1     62440    0.000  0.0000     64972    FALSE   FALSE
     2     58045 4394.299 81.8792     42536     TRUE    TRUE
     3     62434    5.556  0.1035     64803    FALSE   FALSE
     4     62363   76.652  1.4283     65357    FALSE   FALSE
     5     62370   69.564  1.2962     64345     TRUE   FALSE
     6     59780 2659.804 49.5603     49579     TRUE    TRUE
```

Chains 2 and 6 sit 4,394 and 2,660 log-likelihood units below the other four, 50–80
within-chain spreads away, and lower on their own log posterior: `flagged = TRUE`, the
replacement rule would have acted on them during warm-up. Every Rhat is meaningless while
they are there. Under `hardfit()` such chains are replaced at the first burn checks; for a
fit that already has them, drop the flagged chains or refit.

**A subject with two modes.** A 518-subject RDM fit whose rule Rhat passed:

```
Class: region_mode (sample stage, 1400 draws per chain, 6 chains)
Rule Rhat 1.092 (threshold 1.1; plain max 3.036) | min ESS 94 (v_lMd) |
 rhat_b 1.062, rhat_ident 1.029
LL gap 79 (worst chain 1) | subject spread 66.3 (s543; 1 > 5)

Chains (...):          all gaps under 80, none flagged

Subjects with spread > 5 (1):
 subject spread best worst
    s543   66.3    4     5
```

Rhat is met, the chains are within 80 units of each other, and one subject's chains disagree
by 66 units: s543 has two posterior modes and chains 4 and 5 are in different ones. Nothing
at the group level shows it (plain max Rhat 3.0 is this subject). The chains that found the
better mode have the higher log-likelihood for that subject, and the decision is between
seeds, not within one fit:

```{r}
fits <- list(hardfit(emc_a), hardfit(emc_b), hardfit(emc_c))   # three seeds
sapply(fits, function(f) sum(apply(f[[1]]$samples$subj_ll, 1, median)))
```

A seed whose summed log-likelihood sits ten or more units below the best is in a worse mode:
hold it and use the others. No stop rule or chain replacement can fix a case where most
chains sit in the worse mode; several seeds are the only reliable detector.

### Unmet at `max_tries`, still falling

```
Class: ridge_only, rule Rhat still falling ...
Record: met FALSE, tries 40 ...
trace$rule at checks 20, 30, 40: 1.50, 1.42, 1.35
```

`falling = TRUE` means the rule Rhat decreased over the last three checks of an unmet fit:
it is converging slowly, and one continuation (at most two) is worth it. If the Rhat rises
under continuation instead, the problem is structural (`ridge_only` or `region_mode`), not
slow mixing.

## The record

A fit from `hardfit()` carries how it ended:

```{r}
r <- emc[[1]]$stop_record
r$criteria   # the thresholds that were on (NULL = off)
r$met        # TRUE if every criterion passed on one set of draws
r$tries      # checks used since the last restart
r$rule       # the Rhat the rule read at the last check
r$stats      # ess_min, ess_min_par, rhat_b, rhat_ident, ll_gap, ll_z, ll_worst_chain,
             # subj_spread, subj_spread_n5, subj_spread_subject (as d$stats)
r$flat       # the drift statistics (as d$flat)
r$prior      # the prior-tension table (as d$prior)
r$culls      # chains replaced in this call; the list (stage, iteration, chain, donor, gap, z)
             # is emc[[1]]$culls
r$discards   # checks at which the first third was dropped
r$aborted    # NULL, or list(try, rule, abort_gd)
r$restarts   # sample-stage restarts after a replacement
r$trace      # one row per check: try, draws, rule, max_rhat, ess_min, ll_gap,
             # subj_spread, culls, dropped
r$previous   # the record of an earlier hardfit() call on this object
r$time       # minutes
```

`trace` is the progress line as data:

```
   try draws     rule max_rhat  ess_min   ll_gap subj_spread culls dropped
1    1   100 2.126364 8.431421 36.09112 51.20082    5.944289     0       0
2    2   200 2.259881 8.358336 62.02619 65.75251    5.857075     0       0
...
10  10  1000 1.604459 7.766886 73.41182 24.13929    5.266177     0       0
```

## Grading a set of fits

With many fits, grade them from `diagnose()` rather than by eye, and keep the statistics
that explain the grade:

```{r}
grade <- function(f){
  d <- diagnose(f)
  data.frame(class = d$class, falling = d$falling, rule = d$rule$rule,
             ess_min = d$stats$ess_min, rhat_ident = d$stats$rhat_ident,
             ll_gap = d$stats$ll_gap, subj_spread = d$stats$subj_spread,
             flagged = paste(d$chains$chain[d$chains$flagged], collapse = ","))
}
do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, grade))
```

`met` fits are done. `ess_held` and `falling` fits get one continuation. `ridge_only` fits
are reported on their identified quantities. `region_mode` fits with a flagged chain are
refitted; those with a wide subject are compared across seeds on summed log-likelihood.

## What the diagnostics do not tell you

- The prior-tension flag reads one part of the prior: the group means against their prior
  mean and SD (in `type = "single"`, the subject parameters against theirs). The half-t prior
  on the group SDs and the prior on the group correlations have no location to compare
  with, and the subject parameters of a hierarchical fit have no fixed prior at all (their
  prior is the estimated group distribution). A half-t scale far below the true
  between-subject SD shrinks every subject toward the mean and slows the fit in the same way,
  with every group mean inside 3 prior SDs and nothing flagged. For those parts of the prior
  the check is the posterior next to the prior: `plot_pars(emc, selection = "sigma2")` and
  `plot_pars(emc, selection = "correlation")` draw both.
- A single chain can make a long excursion and come back; Rhat over a window can read 1.26
  where Rhat over the whole run reads 1.06. The stop rule reads all kept draws, discards the
  first third only when that alone makes the stop pass, and records when it does.
- The two-mode check needs at least one chain in each mode. With 3 chains a two-mode subject
  goes undetected in a quarter to a third of runs; with 6, about one in ten.

## Why these rules

**Rhat at the .99 quantile.** With hundreds of subjects the plain maximum Rhat is set by one
subject's worst parameter, which can stay above 1.1 for thousands of draws while every group
parameter and 99% of subject parameters have settled. The rule reads the top 1% instead and
every group-level Rhat in full. For `type = "single"` there is no group level and the rule is
the maximum, at 1.05.

**Effective size 100.** Rhat below 1.1 can be reached with 30–60 effective draws, which puts
the Monte Carlo error of a posterior median near a tenth of a posterior SD. In the fits we
checked, 100 is the point beyond which more draws changed no posterior summary, and 200
roughly halved how many fits ever stopped.

**Likelihood gap 100, subject spread 15.** Two chains with the same parameter Rhats but a
likelihood gap of hundreds of units are in different regions of the posterior, usually one
of them degenerate; healthy chains sit within 40 units. A subject whose chains disagree by
more than 15 units has two modes. The chain comparison uses the summed subject
log-likelihood and never the log posterior under pooled group parameters, whose group-density
term differs between healthy chains by hundreds of units; the own-log-posterior guard is
applied only below a gap of 1,000, where it could veto a real difference by noise.

**Replacement, not deletion.** A chain in a degenerate region during warm-up is a bad start
and is replaced from a healthy chain's state, kernel settings included; the posterior is
untouched. In the sample stage a replacement restarts the kept draws, once. Twelve chains
bought nothing over six.

**Early stop at 1.5 after 20 checks.** Of 46 hierarchical and single-subject fits above 1.5
at check 20, none met the rule later.

**Drift is reported, not a stop criterion.** The drift statistics would be the only ones to
notice all chains sliding together along a ridge, with Rhat unaffected; in practice the
slide also makes the autocorrelation enormous, so the effective-size floor fires first.
Their value is in reading an unmet fit.
